messages.content: What is the average price of a 4 ft x 4 ft marble statue in the museum of Philadelphia and 6 ft x 3 ft bronze sculpture in New York museum?

function.name: get_sculpture_details
function.description: Retrieves details of a sculpture, such as its material and size, from a museum database. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

museum_location.description: Location of the museum housing the sculpture.

function.name: get_artwork_price
function.description: Retrieves the price of a sculpture based on size and material. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

museum_location.description: Location of the museum housing the sculpture.

message.reasoning:
We need to compute average price of two sculptures: one 4x4ft marble statue at Museum of Philadelphia; another 6x3ft bronze sculpture in New York museum.

We have tool functions:

get_sculpture_details(museum_location, sculpture_id) -> returns details like material and size.

But we don't know IDs. We might not need them if we can directly use get_artwork_price with location, material, dimensions. But we need material and size first maybe. However question gives us sizes and materials already. So we could call get_artwork_price twice with given data.

However we may need to confirm that those items exist or fetch their details via get_sculpture_details using some known IDs. The user didn't provide IDs. Maybe we assume they want to calculate prices using the pricing function which requires material and size. Since we have both, we can just call get_artwork_price.

Thus we will call get_artwork_price twice:

First: museum_location="Philadelphia", sculpture_material="marble", sculpture_size=[4,4] (assuming square feet). Second: museum_location="New York", sculpture_material="bronze", sculpture_size=[6,3].

Then compute average: (price1 + price2)/2.

We'll need to handle asynchronous calls. We'll produce JSON responses after each function call. Then combine results.
